newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Striking policemen free bank robbers in Brazil.
newsitem.headline: Striking policemen free bank robbers in Brazil.

text.p: Striking policemen, hoping to highlight their demands for months of back pay, released up to 30 bank robbers and other prisoners from jails in northeast Brazil, a newspaper said on Friday.

A police union official in Alagoas state told O Globo newspaper the prisoners were freed because there was no point leaving them in jails that were going to be left unguarded for an unknown amount of time.

The prisoners, who were released on Thursday from 10 jails, were being held for robbing banks, service stations and convenience stores, O Globo said. It said policemen were not respecting a law requiring at least 30 percent of law enforcement officials to remain on duty during strikes.

Telephone calls to police and government offices in the state capital of Maceio went unanswered on Friday as public workers began a second day of work stoppages aimed at pressing officials for pay dating from April.
One Maceio official told O Globo the situation was "almost uncontrollable" as thieves took advantage of the situation to rob banks and stores.
